clue.text: Current topic of commercial interest to the people of Clappham or Streatham?

definitions.text: Current topic of commercial interest to the people of Clappham or Streatham?

parts.note: surface reading: a trade question in the news, as Britain's 1967 bid to join Europe was

parts.words: the people of Clappham or Streatham
parts.note: setter's reading: Clapham and Streatham are London districts each famous for its common, so a market of theirs would be a market for common people

explanation.walkthrough: In 1967 Britain was applying to join the European trading bloc, so it was the current topic; the joke treats its name as a market held on a London common.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Economic Community was popularly called this, a trading bloc of nations sharing tariffs, a big British political issue then.

clue.text: A great man of singular foresight

definitions.text: A great man of singular foresight

parts.words: A great man of singular foresight
parts.note: surface reading: an eminent visionary with rare powers of prediction
setter's reading: a giant of Greek myth
setter's reading: a single eye set in the front of the forehead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' means one, and 'foresight' is sight at the fore: the one-eyed giants of Homer's Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these were huge one-eyed giants, so literally colossal beings with a lone eye in front.

clue.text: He got stuck in his bath

definitions.text: He got stuck in his bath

parts.words: He got stuck in his bath
parts.note: surface reading: someone wedged and unable to climb out of the tub
setter's reading: was stabbed, as a French revolutionary was by Charlotte Corday while bathing in 1793

explanation.walkthrough: The French revolutionary journalist was stabbed to death in his bath, the scene of David's famous painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul, the radical revolutionary leader, was murdered with a knife while soaking in a medicinal tub for a skin disease.

clue.text: Whence comes High Church music?

definitions.text: Whence comes High Church music?

parts.note: surface reading: the elaborate ritual music of Anglo-Catholic worship
setter's reading: high up in a church building, the raised gallery where the instrument is played

explanation.walkthrough: High Church is a style of Anglican worship, but here 'High' just means elevated: the gallery up above the nave.
explanation.definitionFit: This raised gallery in a church houses the pipes and console of the keyboard instrument, so music comes down from it.

clue.text: It's imitation that makes her cry

definitions.text: It's imitation that makes her cry
definitions.note: the clue defines the word as the doll's cry

parts.words: It's imitation that makes her cry
parts.note: surface reading: copying someone has upset a woman
setter's reading: an imitation baby, a talking doll, whose cry calls for its mother

explanation.walkthrough: A doll is an imitation baby, and the classic crying doll says this word, which also names the 'her' of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This childish word for mother is the sound talking dolls were made to say when tipped over.

clue.text: He is expected to make good

definitions.text: He is expected to make good

parts.words: He is expected to make good
parts.note: surface reading: a promising young man who should succeed in life
setter's reading: repair, bring something damaged back to its proper condition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make good' suggests worldly success, but it also means to mend.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who repairs old furniture or paintings returns them to good condition, which is what this tradesman does.

clue.text: Occupant of a walled garden

definitions.text: Occupant of a walled garden
definitions.note: the whole clue: a man's name housed inside the words

indicators.note: an occupant lives inside something, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone living within the walls of an enclosed garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is literally walled in: it lies across the two words, so the only definition is the whole clue's picture of a resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, here pictured as the person residing within the letters of the phrase.

clue.text: You want something hard and shiny? Call up a girl first

definitions.text: something hard and shiny

indicators.note: tells the solver the girl's word stands at the front, before the other piece

parts.note: any girl can be referred to as she

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shop assistant asks whether you want something glossy, then tells you to phone a girl first.
explanation.definitionFit: This resin varnish dries to a tough glossy coat on wood and was once used for gramophone records.

clue.text: "The King thought mair 'marie — Than he listened to the priest"

definitions.text: "The King thought mair 'marie — Than he listened to the priest"
definitions.note: the gap in the quotation is filled by the answer

parts.note: a line from the Scottish ballad of Mary, one of the Queen's four Maries, loved by the king

parts.words: Than he listened to the priest
parts.note: the following line: the king cared more for her than for the clergy's counsel

explanation.walkthrough: The ballad 'The Queen's Maries' runs: 'The King thought mair o' Marie Hamilton Than he listen'd to the priest'. The dash marks her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary of this surname is the doomed lady-in-waiting of the Scottish ballad, hanged for killing her child by the king.

clue.text: Pastimes for which nobody can be entirely unsuited

definitions.text: Pastimes for which nobody can be entirely unsuited

parts.note: surface reading: hobbies that anybody at all can take up
setter's reading: without suits, the hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades held in a hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsuited' means unfit, but a player of bridge or whist always holds some suit in the hand dealt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge, whist and poker are pastimes played with a pack of fifty-two, each hand containing suits.

clue.text: Something serious to send in Kent

definitions.text: Something serious

parts.note: the plain definition: solemn, weighty
setter's hint: add the word send and you have a town on the Thames in Kent

explanation.walkthrough: GRAVE plus SEND makes GRAVESEND, a town in Kent, the county of south-east England; the clue reads like posting something solemn there.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn or weighty matter is described by this adjective, as in a serious situation or a sombre mood.

clue.text: Doesn't a resort change?

definitions.text: a resort

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving six letters

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a seaside town ever alters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian coastal town is a well-known seaside holiday destination and ferry port.

clue.text: Bird smaller than one with a whip

definitions.text: Bird

parts.words: smaller than one with a whip
parts.note: surface reading: a bird outclassed by something carrying a lash
setter's reading: a larger American nightjar whose name is this bird's name with 'whip' put in front

explanation.walkthrough: The poorwill is a small North American nightjar; its relative the whip-poor-will is bigger and carries 'whip' in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A small nightjar of western North America, named after its call, is a genuine species of bird.

clue.text: He was distressed at his betrayal

definitions.text: He was distressed at his betrayal

parts.words: He was distressed at his betrayal
parts.note: surface reading: someone upset at being let down
setter's reading: dis-tressed, robbed of his locks of hair when Delilah betrayed him

explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Delilah had his hair cut off, so he was literally de-tressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical strongman lost his strength when his long hair was shorn after Delilah betrayed him to the Philistines.

clue.text: He goes on working during playtime

definitions.text: He goes on working during playtime

parts.words: He goes on working during playtime
parts.note: surface reading: a diligent pupil who keeps studying through the school break
setter's reading: the time when he plays an instrument, which is his job

explanation.walkthrough: Playtime sounds like a school break, but for this worker playing is the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional performer earns a living by playing an instrument, so play and work are the same thing.

clue.text: As a rule, brooking no opposition

definitions.text: As a rule, brooking no opposition

parts.note: surface reading: usually, generally

parts.words: As a rule, brooking no opposition
parts.note: setter's reading: as a form of rule, a government that tolerates no dissent

explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' looks like 'usually', but it means 'as a kind of government'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannical, autocratic rulers allow nobody to challenge their absolute power, which this adjective describes.

clue.text: A horse below par is still the greatest

definitions.text: the greatest

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece below another simply follows it, so the order of the pieces is set

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a horse is a rider's mount

explanation.surface: A racehorse that is off form remains the champion all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme, foremost, of the highest importance: the adjective names what ranks above everything else.

clue.text: Housman's lad was one

definitions.text: Housman's lad was one

parts.note: surface reading: a young man in A. E. Housman's poetry
setter's reading: the collection is 'A Shropshire Lad', so the lad belonged to that county, whose old name is Salop

explanation.walkthrough: Shropshire is an English county in the West Midlands; its old name Salop gives the word for a native.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or inhabitant of Shropshire is called this, from the county's traditional abbreviated name.

clue.text: Frenchman takes the lead in police investigation

definitions.text: Frenchman
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man from Alsace in eastern France

definitions.text: takes the lead in police investigation
definitions.note: a description of what the dog does, standing for the dog
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a German shepherd dog, walked on a lead by police handlers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the lead' sounds like heading the inquiry, but the dog is literally on a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a native of the French region bordering Germany and the breed British police use as tracker dogs.

clue.text: Not the ways of those who intend to "go straight"

definitions.text: Not the ways of those who intend to "go straight"

parts.note: surface reading: reformed criminals giving up crime
setter's reading: paths that are not straight at all, roundabout routes

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'go straight' invite the ex-convict reading, but literally the ways meant wind about.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare plural noun means circuitous paths or roundabout, evasive ways of talking, the opposite of direct.

clue.text: It's usually got out of a trunk

definitions.text: It's usually got out of a trunk

parts.note: surface reading: something unpacked from a travelling chest
setter's reading: the main stem of a tree, from which limbs grow out

explanation.walkthrough: The trunk is a tree's, not luggage: limbs grow out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb of a tree grows outwards from the main woody stem, so it comes out of the trunk.

clue.text: The loss in reorganising these establishments is apparent

definitions.text: these establishments

indicators.note: reorganising puts things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A business report admits that restructuring these places has cost money.
explanation.definitionFit: Youth hostels and lodging houses are establishments offering cheap accommodation, so they fit as establishments.

clue.text: Can its boys claim to have foresight?

definitions.text: Can its boys claim to have foresight?

parts.note: surface reading: the clever behind-the-scenes boffins and planners
setter's reading: sight to the fore, which a room at the rear cannot have

explanation.walkthrough: 'Backroom boys' are the scientists and planners working out of sight; the joke is that a room at the back cannot see forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear chamber, away from the front, where the backroom boys do their secret research and planning.

clue.text: This Dickensian rogue wore a hood

definitions.text: This Dickensian rogue wore a hood
definitions.note: the clue describes the part of his surname before 'hood'

parts.note: surface reading: a villain in Dickens
setter's reading: the villain's surname is completed by the word hood tacked on the end

explanation.walkthrough: Rogue Riderhood is the waterside villain of Dickens's 'Our Mutual Friend'; his name is RIDER with a hood attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogue Riderhood's surname begins with this word, and 'hood' added to it completes the name of the character.

clue.text: Those who give them are certainly not close-fisted

definitions.text: Those who give them are certainly not close-fisted
definitions.note: the clue defines the plural noun through those who give them

parts.note: surface reading: generous givers, not mean with money
setter's reading: with a clenched fist; these blows are dealt with an open hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Close-fisted' means stingy, but here it is literal: slaps are given open-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaps delivered with the flat of the hand are what this noun means, as in a smack on the bottom.

clue.text: However bad, it has a following in the South of Russia

definitions.text: However bad, it has a following in the South of Russia

parts.words: However bad, it has a following
parts.note: setter's reading: wrongdoing is followed by punishment, as in Dostoevsky's novel title

parts.words: it has a following in the South of Russia
parts.note: setter's reading: follow the word with A and you get the peninsula on the Black Sea

explanation.walkthrough: Dostoevsky's 'Crime and Punishment' gives the following; CRIME followed by A gives CRIMEA, in the south of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoing that breaks the law is punished, so it always has a penalty following it.

clue.text: Hardly the way to describe the "floating population"!

definitions.text: Hardly the way to describe the "floating population"!

parts.note: surface reading: people who move from place to place without a settled home
setter's reading: the froth that literally floats on a liquid's surface, also a contemptuous word for low people

explanation.walkthrough: The word for surface froth is also an insult for the dregs of society, so calling transients this would be rude: 'hardly the way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of dirty froth floats on top of liquid, and figuratively the word means worthless, despised people.

clue.text: Orphaned 28

definitions.text: Orphaned 28
definitions.note: the whole clue: the clue 28 answer bereft of its mothers

indicators.note: an orphan has lost its parents, so the word for mothers is removed

parts.note: the answer to clue 28 across

explanation.walkthrough: Remove MOTHERS from GRANDMOTHERS and you are left with GRAND; the clue has no separate definition, only this deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: The remaining word means magnificent or imposing, and also slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.

clue.text: All in

definitions.text: All in

parts.note: surface reading: exhausted, worn out
setter's reading: everything included, as in an all-in price

explanation.walkthrough: 'All in' first suggests tiredness, but the answer is the sense of a price that covers everything.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-in holiday price covers every cost, so it includes everything with nothing extra to pay.

clue.text: Expert egg-suckers

definitions.text: Expert egg-suckers

parts.note: surface reading: animals such as weasels that raid nests
setter's reading: the old saying about not teaching an elderly relative to suck eggs, since she already knows how

explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't teach your grandmother to suck eggs' means don't instruct someone more experienced, so these are the experts.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb assumes old women are already masters of egg-sucking, so they need no lessons from the young.
